note: The crop regions a correct figure stage arrives at for this paper. No PNG is committed (bundles are not), so this file is what a run compares its own boxes against: crop.py cuts the same pixels from a 150 DPI render given these boxes and this space. Neither exhibit has an OCR proposal behind it, because the figure is drawn as vector art and tables are never proposed, so both regions were located from the render with the text layer's own bboxes as the starting point.
space: Boxes are in the PDF page space in points, the size blocks.json records for the page. Hand it to crop.py as --space and the tool maps the boxes into render pixels; never scale them by hand.

exhibits.label: table_01
exhibits.includes: the top rule, which the caption sits directly above, the header row and its rule, the three body rows, the bottom rule, and the printed footnote line
exhibits.excludes: the caption, which belongs to text.md, and the paragraphs above and below the float

exhibits.label: figure_01
exhibits.includes: the figure's own printed title, the legend riding beside it, both axes with their tick labels, the twelve bars, and the axis label under them
exhibits.excludes: the caption below the figure, which belongs to text.md

supplement_a.note: The crop region for Supplement A's only exhibit, in the supplement's own PDF rather than the paper's. The region starts above the table's top rule and ends below its printed footnote, both of which are part of the exhibit, and stops short of the caption, which belongs to the supplement's text.md.

exhibits.label: supplement_a_table_01
exhibits.includes: the top rule, both header rows with the span rules that tie each group name to its pair of columns, the four station rows including the two cells the survey left empty, the bottom rule, and the printed footnote line
exhibits.excludes: the caption above the top rule, which belongs to the supplement's text.md, and the running head and intro paragraph above it
